decisions.title: Stable scope is XML Schema 1.0 Second Edition
decisions.issue: XML Schema 1.1 adds assertions, alternatives, open content, and datatype changes that cannot be accepted partially without changing parsing, compilation, validation, and interoperability behavior.
interpretations: Track the latest W3C schema vocabulary; accept recognizable 1.1 syntax as foreign markup; implement isolated 1.1 features under the 1.0 claim; or close the stable language to 1.0 Second Edition plus reviewed errata.
decisions.peer_behavior: JAXP and other validators expose different 1.0 and 1.1 support levels. Peer acceptance therefore does not identify this package's selected feature line.
decisions.selected_behavior: Stable support is exactly XML Schema 1.0 Second Edition plus the pinned errata snapshot. XML Schema 1.1 syntax and semantics are rejected or retained only where 1.0 explicitly permits foreign annotation content; no partial 1.1 conformance is advertised.
decisions.rationale: Stable support is exactly XML Schema 1.0 Second Edition plus the pinned errata snapshot. XML Schema 1.1 syntax and semantics are rejected or retained only where 1.0 explicitly permits foreign annotation content; no partial 1.1 conformance is advertised.
decisions.security_consequences: A closed grammar prevents unreviewed assertions or alternative-selection languages from introducing executable or amplified work. Existing parser, compiler, and validator limits cover the selected 1.0 model.
decisions.resource_consequences: A closed grammar prevents unreviewed assertions or alternative-selection languages from introducing executable or amplified work. Existing parser, compiler, and validator limits cover the selected 1.0 model.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: XML Schema 1.0 documents have a stable interpretation. A 1.1 document cannot silently downgrade over the wire and requires a future explicit feature-line API and migration review.
decisions.wire_consequences: XML Schema 1.0 documents have a stable interpretation. A 1.1 document cannot silently downgrade over the wire and requires a future explicit feature-line API and migration review.
decisions.upstream_status: Exact W3C publications, errata snapshot, schema resources, and XSTS archive are pinned in the manifest.
decisions.reconsider_when: XML Schema 1.1 is selected as a separately complete, tested, and documented feature line.

decisions.title: Parsing performs no external resolution
decisions.issue: Includes, imports, and redefines name external resources, but the specification does not define application trust, filesystem roots, network policy, credentials, redirects, or cancellation. Implicit parser I/O would embed unsafe deployment policy.
interpretations: Resolve locations while parsing; allow file and HTTP URLs by default; ignore composition references; use a process-global catalog; or preserve references and require an injected bounded resolver during compilation.
decisions.peer_behavior: Validators often expose parser-specific entity and schema-resolution callbacks, with defaults varying by runtime and deployment. Those defaults are not portable security policy.
decisions.selected_behavior: Parsing consumes only caller-supplied bytes and retains composition references. Compilation resolves them only through an injected `resolve.Resolver`; the default deny resolver permits no file or network access. The opt-in file resolver is root-confined and byte-bounded.
decisions.rationale: Parsing consumes only caller-supplied bytes and retains composition references. Compilation resolves them only through an injected `resolve.Resolver`; the default deny resolver permits no file or network access. The opt-in file resolver is root-confined and byte-bounded.
decisions.security_consequences: Default parsing and compilation have no SSRF, credential forwarding, DNS, redirect, or path-traversal side effects. Injected resolvers remain caller-owned trust boundaries subject to graph, byte, depth, reference, and context limits.
decisions.resource_consequences: Default parsing and compilation have no SSRF, credential forwarding, DNS, redirect, or path-traversal side effects. Injected resolvers remain caller-owned trust boundaries subject to graph, byte, depth, reference, and context limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Resource identities remain explicit URIs in the model; bytes are never fetched merely because a schema arrived over a wire. Callers must provide identical resolver inputs for reproducible compilation.
decisions.wire_consequences: Resource identities remain explicit URIs in the model; bytes are never fetched merely because a schema arrived over a wire. Callers must provide identical resolver inputs for reproducible compilation.
decisions.upstream_status: Resolution requirements are mapped as `DOC-003`, `DOC-004`, and `RES-001` in `specification/requirements/xsd-1.0.tsv`.
decisions.reconsider_when: A new explicit resolver adapter is added; parsing itself remains I/O-free unless the public ownership contract is deliberately redesigned.

decisions.title: Conformance claims require matrix evidence
decisions.issue: A green unit suite or raw XSTS percentage does not prove every broad feature claim. XSTS also contains `queried` expectations that are not accepted pass/fail requirements.
interpretations: Claim support from implementation presence; ignore XSTS; count queried expectations as passes or failures; use only aggregate percentages; or require each normative matrix row to name focused evidence and applicable official expectations.
decisions.peer_behavior: Validators report XSTS with different harnesses, exclusions, and feature lines. Counts are comparable only when the archive, expectation policy, and denominator match.
decisions.selected_behavior: A feature is supported only when its versioned requirement row names the normative source and executable evidence covering the stated scope. Official fixtures supplement that mapping; a green unit suite or aggregate percentage cannot replace it.
decisions.rationale: A feature is supported only when its versioned requirement row names the normative source and executable evidence covering the stated scope. Official fixtures supplement that mapping; a green unit suite or aggregate percentage cannot replace it.
decisions.security_consequences: The harness confines resources to the extracted suite root and applies normal compiler and validator limits. A fixture cannot authorize network or filesystem access outside that root.
decisions.resource_consequences: The harness confines resources to the extracted suite root and applies normal compiler and validator limits. A fixture cannot authorize network or filesystem access outside that root.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Conformance claims are attributable to exact schema and instance fixtures rather than an opaque percentage. A newly discovered semantic gap reopens its row instead of narrowing prose or accepting divergent wire behavior.
decisions.wire_consequences: Conformance claims are attributable to exact schema and instance fixtures rather than an opaque percentage. A newly discovered semantic gap reopens its row instead of narrowing prose or accepting divergent wire behavior.
public_apis: Published XML Schema 1.0 support claims and all APIs covered by `specification/requirements/xsd-1.0.tsv`
decisions.upstream_status: Requirement status and evidence remain in `specification/requirements/xsd-1.0.tsv`; the measured corpus result is retained in `xsts-baseline.md`.
decisions.reconsider_when: A requirement row, corpus pin, or accepted-expectation policy changes.

decisions.title: XSTS baseline bounds the conformance claim
decisions.issue: A complete pass over accepted XSTS expectations is a point-in-time corpus result, not proof of every XML Schema behavior or future correctness.
interpretations: Claim universal conformance from the corpus; report only a percentage; freeze completed labels; or bind the exact corpus result to only the documented matrix rows it exercises.
decisions.peer_behavior: Validators publish support matrices with different update and regression policies. A historical peer claim does not prove current behavior.
decisions.selected_behavior: The recorded baseline reports 24,696 accepted XSTS expectations passing without skips and 90 upstream `queried` expectations separately. It supports only the documented matrix rows it exercises. Any semantic gap or regression reopens its affected row; XSTS success is never described as universal XSD conformance.
decisions.rationale: The recorded baseline reports 24,696 accepted XSTS expectations passing without skips and 90 upstream `queried` expectations separately. It supports only the documented matrix rows it exercises. Any semantic gap or regression reopens its affected row; XSTS success is never described as universal XSD conformance.
decisions.security_consequences: Fail-closed reopening prevents security and resource regressions from being relabeled as unsupported edge cases. Official execution remains root-confined and bounded.
decisions.resource_consequences: Fail-closed reopening prevents security and resource regressions from being relabeled as unsupported edge cases. Official execution remains root-confined and bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Accepted schema and instance wire behavior cannot be narrowed silently to preserve a green status. A changed support row requires explicit compatibility and changelog review.
decisions.wire_consequences: Accepted schema and instance wire behavior cannot be narrowed silently to preserve a green status. A changed support row requires explicit compatibility and changelog review.
public_apis: Published XML Schema 1.0 matrix and XSTS baseline claims
decisions.upstream_status: Current row status is retained in `specification/requirements/xsd-1.0.tsv`; exact corpus counts are retained in `xsts-baseline.md`.
decisions.reconsider_when: Any requirement evidence, accepted fixture, implementation behavior, or corpus pin changes.

decisions.title: Normative-source precedence and errata
decisions.issue: Prose, schema-for-schemas, primer examples, errata, XSTS expectations, and implementations can disagree. Treating all artifacts as equally normative creates circular or fixture-driven behavior.
interpretations: Follow the schema-for-schemas mechanically; use XSTS as the specification; copy JAXP behavior; ignore errata; or apply normative prose plus accepted errata and classify every lower-authority disagreement.
decisions.peer_behavior: Independent validators differ around errata and under-specified edge cases. A peer majority is evidence to investigate, not authority over W3C normative text.
decisions.selected_behavior: Structures and Datatypes normative prose, as corrected by the pinned Second Edition errata, controls. The schema-for-schemas constrains syntax only where the recommendation assigns that role. Primer, examples, XSTS, and peer output are evidence and cannot silently override prose.
decisions.rationale: Structures and Datatypes normative prose, as corrected by the pinned Second Edition errata, controls. The schema-for-schemas constrains syntax only where the recommendation assigns that role. Primer, examples, XSTS, and peer output are evidence and cannot silently override prose.
decisions.security_consequences: Explicit precedence prevents permissive fixtures or generated schemas from weakening validation. All accepted interpretations still execute under package resource limits.
decisions.resource_consequences: Explicit precedence prevents permissive fixtures or generated schemas from weakening validation. All accepted interpretations still execute under package resource limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Contradictions resolve deterministically and are documented before changing accepted schema or instance wire data. A changed erratum interpretation receives compatibility review.
decisions.wire_consequences: Contradictions resolve deterministically and are documented before changing accepted schema or instance wire data. A changed erratum interpretation receives compatibility review.
public_apis: All parsing, compilation, validation, datatype, and serialization behavior
decisions.upstream_status: Source role, version, status, digest, size, and URL are recorded independently in the manifest.
decisions.reconsider_when: W3C publishes a superseding correction or a minimized fixture proves the selected reading conflicts with normative prose.

decisions.title: DTD and entity processing is forbidden
decisions.issue: XML permits DTD declarations and entities, but XML Schema processing does not require this package to expose entity expansion. Accepting them introduces external-resource, amplification, and parser-differential risks.
interpretations: Delegate all XML behavior to the host decoder; allow internal entities only; expand with limits; ignore declarations; or reject every DTD before schema or instance processing.
decisions.peer_behavior: XML parsers and schema validators differ in entity defaults and hardening flags. Secure deployment guidance commonly disables DTDs, but defaults remain runtime-specific.
decisions.selected_behavior: Schema parsing and instance validation reject any DTD directive before component or instance processing and never expand external entities. This is a deliberate secure profile layered on XML Schema 1.0.
decisions.rationale: Schema parsing and instance validation reject any DTD directive before component or instance processing and never expand external entities. This is a deliberate secure profile layered on XML Schema 1.0.
decisions.security_consequences: Rejection removes XXE, external fetch, and entity-expansion amplification from owned parsing paths. Input bytes, element depth, nodes, text, and diagnostics remain independently bounded.
decisions.resource_consequences: Rejection removes XXE, external fetch, and entity-expansion amplification from owned parsing paths. Input bytes, element depth, nodes, text, and diagnostics remain independently bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Schema or instance wire documents requiring DTD entities are rejected rather than normalized. Callers must resolve trusted entities before this boundary if their application deliberately supports them.
decisions.wire_consequences: Schema or instance wire documents requiring DTD entities are rejected rather than normalized. Callers must resolve trusted entities before this boundary if their application deliberately supports them.
public_apis: `Parse`, `validate.Validator`, byte, reader, and tree validation entry points
decisions.upstream_status: The secure profile is mapped as `SEC-001` and `SEC-002` in the requirement matrix.
decisions.reconsider_when: No implicit DTD mode is planned; any future opt-in would require a separate threat model and feature-line contract.

decisions.title: Expanded names own identity
decisions.specification: W3C Namespaces in XML 1.0 Third Edition
decisions.issue: Prefixes are lexical aliases, while component identity uses namespace URI plus local name. Includes without a target namespace acquire the including schema's namespace, and serialization may need to allocate new prefixes.
interpretations: Treat prefixes as identity; preserve only lexical QName text; reject chameleon includes; use one process-global prefix map; or resolve expanded names in scope and allocate deterministic serialization prefixes.
decisions.peer_behavior: Validators agree on expanded-name identity but may preserve or regenerate prefixes differently. Byte-identical prefix output is not a normative validation requirement.
decisions.selected_behavior: Parsing resolves QName-valued attributes against their local namespace scope. Compilation keys components by expanded name and applies chameleon namespaces to included no-namespace schemas. Serialization preserves semantic expanded names and allocates deterministic prefixes when needed.
decisions.rationale: Parsing resolves QName-valued attributes against their local namespace scope. Compilation keys components by expanded name and applies chameleon namespaces to included no-namespace schemas. Serialization preserves semantic expanded names and allocates deterministic prefixes when needed.
decisions.security_consequences: Namespace and component counts are bounded, unknown prefixes fail closed, and no prefix text can shadow a different namespace identity. Serialization work and output remain bounded.
decisions.resource_consequences: Namespace and component counts are bounded, unknown prefixes fail closed, and no prefix text can shadow a different namespace identity. Serialization work and output remain bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Different valid prefixes compile to the same component identity. Serialized bytes may use deterministic package-selected prefixes while preserving equivalent namespace wire semantics.
decisions.wire_consequences: Different valid prefixes compile to the same component identity. Serialized bytes may use deterministic package-selected prefixes while preserving equivalent namespace wire semantics.
public_apis: `QName`, parsed `Document`, `compile.Set`, component lookup, builders, and serialization
decisions.upstream_status: Namespace, composition, and chameleon obligations are mapped under `DOC-004`, `COMP-002`, and `COMP-003`.
decisions.reconsider_when: A lexical-preservation mode is introduced; semantic identity remains expanded-name based.

decisions.title: XML Schema regular expressions are a distinct dialect
decisions.issue: XML Schema regexes are implicitly unanchored in their own grammar and differ from Go RE2, PCRE, and ECMAScript in subtraction, escapes, character classes, and matching semantics. Direct host-regex compilation changes accepted values.
interpretations: Pass patterns directly to Go `regexp`; use the ECMAScript package; support a convenient subset silently; or parse and translate the exact XML Schema 1.0 dialect with bounded expansion and explicit rejection.
decisions.peer_behavior: General-purpose regex engines expose different syntax and anchoring. XML Schema validators implement a dedicated dialect or translation layer.
decisions.selected_behavior: Pattern facets use the XML Schema 1.0 regex grammar and matching semantics. Translation to the execution engine is bounded, class subtraction and escapes retain XSD meaning, derived pattern facets remain cumulative, and invalid expressions fail compilation.
decisions.rationale: Pattern facets use the XML Schema 1.0 regex grammar and matching semantics. Translation to the execution engine is bounded, class subtraction and escapes retain XSD meaning, derived pattern facets remain cumulative, and invalid expressions fail compilation.
decisions.security_consequences: Translation width, range expansion, pattern size, and execution work are bounded before amplification. Unsupported or malformed syntax fails closed rather than reaching a permissive host engine.
decisions.resource_consequences: Translation width, range expansion, pattern size, and execution work are bounded before amplification. Unsupported or malformed syntax fails closed rather than reaching a permissive host engine.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Pattern facet wire text is interpreted as XSD regex, never Go, PCRE, or ECMAScript. Equivalent host-engine strings are not a compatibility guarantee.
decisions.wire_consequences: Pattern facet wire text is interpreted as XSD regex, never Go, PCRE, or ECMAScript. Equivalent host-engine strings are not a compatibility guarantee.
public_apis: Pattern facets, datatype compilation, schema compilation, and instance validation
decisions.upstream_status: Pattern support is mapped under `TYPE-002` in the requirement matrix.
decisions.reconsider_when: XML Schema 1.1 is implemented or the execution backend changes; the public dialect remains versioned XSD syntax.

decisions.title: Identity constraints use only the XSD XPath subset
decisions.issue: `xs:selector` and `xs:field` use a restricted XPath grammar, not general XPath. Delegating to a full engine accepts functions, axes, and expressions the schema language forbids and can add unbounded work.
interpretations: Run XPath 1.0; accept any host-engine expression; implement string matching heuristics; or parse only the specification subset and estimate every evaluation step.
decisions.peer_behavior: Schema validators implement the restricted selector and field grammar, though diagnostics and extension behavior differ. General XPath libraries intentionally accept much more.
decisions.selected_behavior: The compiler accepts exactly the XML Schema 1.0 selector and field subset, including namespace-qualified names and permitted descendant forms. Validation evaluates that compiled subset with explicit node, identity-value, step, and diagnostic limits.
decisions.rationale: The compiler accepts exactly the XML Schema 1.0 selector and field subset, including namespace-qualified names and permitted descendant forms. Validation evaluates that compiled subset with explicit node, identity-value, step, and diagnostic limits.
decisions.security_consequences: No XPath functions, arbitrary axes, extension callbacks, or implicit I/O execute. Step accounting bounds amplification across large trees and key tables.
decisions.resource_consequences: No XPath functions, arbitrary axes, extension callbacks, or implicit I/O execute. Step accounting bounds amplification across large trees and key tables.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Unsupported general XPath wire expressions are schema errors rather than implementation extensions. Valid selectors compare expanded names using in-scope namespaces.
decisions.wire_consequences: Unsupported general XPath wire expressions are schema errors rather than implementation extensions. Valid selectors compare expanded names using in-scope namespaces.
public_apis: Parsed identity constraints, compiler plans, and validation of `unique`, `key`, and `keyref`
decisions.upstream_status: Identity requirements are mapped as `IDENT-001` and `IDENT-002`.
decisions.reconsider_when: A future XML Schema feature line defines a different selector language.

decisions.title: Datatype comparisons use value spaces
decisions.issue: Lexically different values can be equal after whitespace, numeric, QName, calendar, duration, list, union, or derived-type processing. Byte-string equality gives incorrect fixed values, identity constraints, facets, and canonical forms.
interpretations: Compare source text; normalize all values as strings; use host floating-point and time types; or parse each built-in and derived datatype into its XML Schema value space before equality and ordering.
decisions.peer_behavior: Conforming validators compare value spaces, but host numeric, calendar, timezone, and QName representations can create implementation-specific edge cases.
decisions.selected_behavior: Whitespace applies before other facets, arbitrary-precision decimal and integer values remain exact, QName values include namespace context, list and union members retain selected types, and fixed values and identity keys compare in the declared value space. Partial calendar ordering remains explicit rather than coerced to host time.
decisions.rationale: Whitespace applies before other facets, arbitrary-precision decimal and integer values remain exact, QName values include namespace context, list and union members retain selected types, and fixed values and identity keys compare in the declared value space. Partial calendar ordering remains explicit rather than coerced to host time.
decisions.security_consequences: Lexical bytes, numeric digits, list members, union candidates, and comparison work are bounded. Exact arithmetic avoids overflow and lossy security decisions.
decisions.resource_consequences: Lexical bytes, numeric digits, list members, union candidates, and comparison work are bounded. Exact arithmetic avoids overflow and lossy security decisions.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Canonically different XML lexical forms may validate as equal; namespace context can make identical QName text unequal. Diagnostics preserve source locations without redefining wire values.
decisions.wire_consequences: Canonically different XML lexical forms may validate as equal; namespace context can make identical QName text unequal. Diagnostics preserve source locations without redefining wire values.
public_apis: Datatype parsing, facets, fixed/default constraints, identity constraints, and validation diagnostics
decisions.upstream_status: Datatype obligations are mapped under `TYPE-001` through `TYPE-003`.
decisions.reconsider_when: A datatype defect, erratum, or future feature line changes value-space semantics.

decisions.title: Deterministic serialization preserves schema semantics
decisions.issue: XML Schema defines semantic XML, not one byte serialization. Namespace declaration order, generated prefixes, attribute order, annotation markup, and empty values can vary or be lost during model round trips.
interpretations: Preserve original bytes; emit host encoder output; discard annotation markup; claim canonical XML; or define a deterministic package profile that preserves represented semantics without claiming W3C canonicalization.
decisions.peer_behavior: Validators commonly regenerate semantically equivalent schemas with different prefixes and formatting. Byte identity is not required for schema validity.
decisions.selected_behavior: Serialization preflights the complete model, emits deterministic UTF-8 XML, sorts namespace declarations, allocates stable prefixes, preserves empty constraints, IDs, annotations, and supported component families, and rejects unknown QName namespaces or cyclic models. It is deterministic package output, not Canonical XML.
decisions.rationale: Serialization preflights the complete model, emits deterministic UTF-8 XML, sorts namespace declarations, allocates stable prefixes, preserves empty constraints, IDs, annotations, and supported component families, and rejects unknown QName namespaces or cyclic models. It is deterministic package output, not Canonical XML.
decisions.security_consequences: Preflight bounds depth, components, retained memory, and output bytes before partial writes. Unsafe annotation fragments, cycles, unknown namespaces, and write failures fail explicitly.
decisions.resource_consequences: Preflight bounds depth, components, retained memory, and output bytes before partial writes. Unsafe annotation fragments, cycles, unknown namespaces, and write failures fail explicitly.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Parse-marshal round trips preserve represented schema semantics but not original whitespace or prefix spelling. Repeated serialization of the same model produces stable package bytes.
decisions.wire_consequences: Parse-marshal round trips preserve represented schema semantics but not original whitespace or prefix spelling. Repeated serialization of the same model produces stable package bytes.
decisions.upstream_status: Serialization policy is mapped as `SER-001` and `SER-002`.
decisions.reconsider_when: A separate lexical-preserving or standards-defined canonicalization mode is introduced.

decisions.title: Finite limits and structured diagnostics are observable policy
decisions.issue: The specifications define validity but not finite Go process budgets, cancellation granularity, diagnostic caps, or ownership. Recursive schemas, particles, XPath selectors, and invalid instances can amplify work and errors.
interpretations: Apply no limits; return only the first error; collect every diagnostic; use hidden worker goroutines for deadlines; or expose finite limits and deterministic typed failures at every stage.
decisions.peer_behavior: Validators apply implementation-specific recursion, memory, and error-count limits. Their thresholds and diagnostic wording are not normative.
decisions.selected_behavior: Parse, compile, validate, serialize, resolver, regex, identity, and diagnostic work is bounded by explicit options with conservative defaults. Context cancellation is checked synchronously. Validation distinguishes structured invalidity diagnostics from parser, resource, cancellation, and I/O errors.
decisions.rationale: Parse, compile, validate, serialize, resolver, regex, identity, and diagnostic work is bounded by explicit options with conservative defaults. Context cancellation is checked synchronously. Validation distinguishes structured invalidity diagnostics from parser, resource, cancellation, and I/O errors.
decisions.security_consequences: Every untrusted amplification dimension has checked finite accounting; diagnostic growth cannot consume unbounded memory. No hidden worker is required for owned cancellation.
decisions.resource_consequences: Every untrusted amplification dimension has checked finite accounting; diagnostic growth cannot consume unbounded memory. No hidden worker is required for owned cancellation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: A valid schema or instance may return a resource error under a selected policy even when an unconstrained validator would finish. Remote callers requiring identical outcomes must carry equivalent limit configuration explicitly.
decisions.wire_consequences: A valid schema or instance may return a resource error under a selected policy even when an unconstrained validator would finish. Remote callers requiring identical outcomes must carry equivalent limit configuration explicitly.
public_apis: All options and limits, typed errors, `Result.Diagnostics`, resolvers, parsers, compilers, validators, and serializers
decisions.upstream_status: Defensive requirements are mapped as `SEC-003`, `SEC-004`, `VAL-003`, and `SER-002`.
decisions.reconsider_when: A stage gains new recursive, allocating, I/O, or diagnostic behavior.

decisions.title: Byte, reader, and tree validation share one semantic engine
decisions.issue: Separate byte, streaming-reader, and caller-owned tree validators can diverge in namespace context, DTD rejection, limits, diagnostics, or mutation ownership.
interpretations: Maintain independent implementations; normalize every input to bytes; mutate caller trees for annotations; give streaming weaker limits; or route all forms through one validation plan with representation-specific bounded ingestion.
decisions.peer_behavior: Validation libraries expose different combinations of DOM and streaming APIs, often with distinct diagnostics and ownership rules. The specification does not choose a Go representation.
decisions.selected_behavior: Byte, incremental reader, and caller-owned tree entry points share the same compiled validation engine and semantic outcomes. Each path enforces owned input bounds, rejects DTDs, preserves namespace context, does not mutate caller trees, and returns the same structured diagnostic model.
decisions.rationale: Byte, incremental reader, and caller-owned tree entry points share the same compiled validation engine and semantic outcomes. Each path enforces owned input bounds, rejects DTDs, preserves namespace context, does not mutate caller trees, and returns the same structured diagnostic model.
decisions.security_consequences: Reader bytes, tree nodes, attributes, text, namespace data, and semantic work are bounded before retention or traversal. Caller resources are not closed or mutated implicitly.
decisions.resource_consequences: Reader bytes, tree nodes, attributes, text, namespace data, and semantic work are bounded before retention or traversal. Caller resources are not closed or mutated implicitly.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Equivalent XML information produces equivalent validation regardless of entry point. Reader chunking and in-memory tree layout do not become wire-visible semantics.
decisions.wire_consequences: Equivalent XML information produces equivalent validation regardless of entry point. Reader chunking and in-memory tree layout do not become wire-visible semantics.
decisions.upstream_status: Validation-mode parity is mapped as `VAL-001`, `VAL-002`, and `QUAL-004`.
decisions.reconsider_when: A new input representation or truly incremental output API is added.
